newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian charged with Thai prostitution racket.
newsitem.headline: Australian charged with Thai prostitution racket.

text.p: An Australian man appeared in court on Monday charged with organising an international prostitution racket involving Thai women who were brought to Australia illegally and forced to work as prostitutes.

Van Chau Le, 37, an Australian citizen of Vietnamese origin, appeared in the Melbourne Magistrates Court to face eight charges, including issuing fake Australian visitor visas and living off the earnings of a prostitute.

An immigration official told Reuters that five Thai women in custody were being questioned over immigration law violations after police and immigration officers raided three brothels during the weekend. Le, who was remanded in custody until December 16, was arrested during the raids.
Outside the court, Australian Federal Police officer Peter Fennell said between 20 and 30 women aged in their twenties had been brought to Australia from Thailand to work in brothels.

Melbourne's The Age newspaper on Monday quoted police sources as saying that the women were brought to Australia on false Thai passports, but after entering the country had their passports taken from them and were forced to work in brothels.
The women were forced to hand over earnings of A$30,000 to A$35,000 (US$24,300-$28,350) before their passports were returned, The Age said.
Fennell told reporters that investigations were continuing in Australia and overseas, with more charges expected.
